Reconstruction depth
A fixed-point value stores an integer together with an implied scale , so the represented real quantity is

For a binary fractional format with fractional bits, . Increasing improves resolution but consumes integer range because storage width has not changed. For signed -bit two’s-complement storage, the approximate real range is

This makes format choice an error-budget decision rather than a syntax decision. Position data may need large range; normalized coefficients may need fine local resolution. Multiplication temporarily doubles the number of fractional bits, so a production operation needs a widened intermediate or a deliberate rescale, round and saturate policy.

Tests should exercise representable endpoints, half-step rounding, overflow, negative values, multiplication rescaling and accumulation. A format can be perfectly deterministic and still be numerically unsuitable if its step size exceeds the physical or visual tolerance of the subsystem using it.

Appendix.title: UNORM and SNORM
Appendix.Content: UNORM and SNORM
Curriculum depth: Developed · First seen: C006 · Latest development: C006
Definition and mechanism
UNORM decodes q/(2^n-1); UNORM8 code128 gives128/255. SNORM commonly clamps q/(2^(n-1)-1) at -1, so -128 and -127 both map to -1 for eight bits.
Prerequisites

ListItem.Content: • Affine quantization and zero point — supplies the representation or validity rule used above.

Reconstruction depth
An -bit UNORM integer represents a real value approximately in through

Quantization reverses that map with a declared rounding rule and saturation. The endpoint denominator matters: dividing by would make the largest code fail to represent exactly . This is why a normalized color channel can round-trip its endpoints even though most interior values incur quantization error.

SNORM maps a signed integer code to approximately . APIs differ in how the most-negative integer is treated, so the format specification—not intuition—owns the exact decode rule. This matters for normals and tangent vectors: decoding produces components, not a guaranteed unit vector. A sampled normal map usually requires later reconstruction or normalization and a coordinate-space convention.

A useful test suite checks endpoint codes, monotonicity, round-trip error bounds, saturation outside the nominal domain, and the API’s exact most-negative SNORM behavior. Treating UNORM/SNORM as small floats hides where nonlinear color encoding, signed-vector normalization, and integer filtering contracts actually enter.

Appendix.Content: Binary16

Reconstruction depth

IEEE binary16 uses 1 sign bit, 5 exponent bits and 10 stored fraction bits. Normal numbers have an implicit leading one, giving 11 bits of significand precision. The narrow exponent and significand make half precision cheaper to store and move than binary32, but not a drop-in replacement for every intermediate.

Around magnitude 1, adjacent normal values are roughly apart. As magnitude grows, spacing grows with the exponent. Subnormals extend representable values toward zero with reduced precision, while exponent all-ones encodes infinities and NaNs.

A graphics or ML pipeline should distinguish storage precision from accumulation precision. Vertex attributes, textures or weights may be stored as binary16 while dot products and reductions accumulate in binary32. This often preserves bandwidth savings without accepting catastrophic accumulation error.

Tests should include exact endpoints around 1, overflow to infinity according to conversion rules, underflow and subnormals, signed zero and NaN propagation policy. Hardware may flush subnormals or use mixed-precision instructions, so performance behavior requires target-specific evidence.

Appendix.title: Bfloat16
Appendix.Content: Bfloat16
Curriculum depth: Developed · First seen: C006 · Latest development: C006
Definition and mechanism
BF16 has1/8/7 fields, bias127 and8 normal precision bits. It keeps broad exponent range at coarse spacing2^-7 above1. A nearest-even conversion must handle NaNs separately from finite rounding.
Prerequisites

ListItem.Content: • IEEE-754 floating point — supplies the representation or validity rule used above.
• Rounding to nearest ties to even — supplies the representation or validity rule used above.

Source and navigation
Continuous teaching story · Source coverage ledger · Dependency Map
Range is preserved more than precision

Bfloat16 keeps the 8-bit exponent width of binary32 but stores only 7 explicit fraction bits. A normal value therefore has 8 bits of significand precision including the hidden leading one. Compared with IEEE binary16, bfloat16 sacrifices substantial local precision to retain a binary32-like exponent range.

That trade is useful for ML tensors whose dynamic range matters more than fine per-value precision. It is poor for algorithms where small relative changes accumulate over many steps. Common mixed-precision kernels store operands in bfloat16 but accumulate products in binary32.

Conversion is not merely truncation if the implementation promises round-to-nearest behavior. Correct rounding must account for discarded bits and tie policy; NaN payloads and infinities need explicit handling. Tests should inspect bit-level round trips, halfway cases, overflow/underflow, NaNs, and error growth in dot products accumulated in bfloat16 versus binary32.

Appendix.title: Checksums CRCs and hashes
Appendix.Content: Checksums, CRCs, and hashes
Curriculum depth: Reference implemented and known-answer tested · First seen: C006 · Latest development: Phase 28 repair
A checksum or digest maps an arbitrary byte sequence to a smaller fixed-size value. Different families make different promises.
An additive checksum is mainly an accidental-error detector and is weak against structured changes such as reordering or compensating byte modifications.

A CRC interprets bits as a polynomial over and computes a remainder under a declared generator polynomial and parameter set. CRCs are excellent for many transmission/storage error patterns, but they are not cryptographic authenticators.

A cryptographic hash such as SHA-256 is designed so that finding collisions or preimages is computationally hard under the security assumptions of the primitive. A hash still does not authenticate a file when an attacker can replace both the file and the untrusted hash value.
SHA-256 compression structure

SHA-256 pads the message with a one bit, enough zero bits to leave 64 bits at the end of the final 512-bit block, and then the original message length modulo . Each 512-bit block expands sixteen 32-bit words into a 64-word schedule and updates an eight-word chaining state through 64 rounds.

The important learning boundary is representation: message words are interpreted in the algorithm’s specified byte order. Reinterpreting native host integers without explicit conversion can produce a platform-specific hash implementation.
Known-answer evidence

tools/labs/crypto_primitives_lab.cpp implements SHA-256 directly and validates the standard digest of “abc” and the empty message. The same SHA-256 implementation is then used by HMAC, HKDF and a domain-separated Merkle tree.

This raises the evidence above “definition present,” but the implementation is educational. It is not reviewed for constant-time behavior, hardware acceleration, fault attacks, side channels or production cryptographic use.
What to use for what
Use a checksum/CRC when the threat is accidental corruption and the protocol specifies the polynomial/parameters.
Use a cryptographic hash when content identity or collision/preimage resistance is required.
Use a MAC such as HMAC when a party holding a secret key must authenticate content.
Use a digital signature when verification must be possible without sharing the signing secret.
Prerequisites
Bitwise XOR, Serialization, Endianness.
Used by
Integrity and authenticity, HMAC and HKDF, Merkle trees and authenticated structure, Production manifests and transactional publication.

Appendix.title: Linear systems and fundamental subspaces
Appendix.Content: Linear systems and fundamental subspaces

A linear system asks which inputs satisfy all row measurements at once. It is consistent exactly when lies in the column space. The null space contains input changes invisible to every measurement; rank-nullity counts observable versus free directions.
Use it when: explaining consistency, underdetermination, least squares, parameter observability, or constraints in geometry.

Developed in Phase 8: The expanded treatment connects each row to a hyperplane and the complete matrix to a map: consistency asks whether the target lies in the column space, while the null space describes every invisible change to a solution. Rank then counts constrained directions and determines the dimension of the solution family. constraint geometry · rank and solution families
Prerequisites
Matrices as linear maps and basis images, Basis coordinates and dimension, Projection rejection and scalar components.
Used by

Appendix.title: Gaussian elimination and pivoting
Appendix.Content: Gaussian elimination and pivoting

Use it when: understanding REF/RREF, LU, consistency, rank, and triangular solves.

Developed in Phase 8: Elimination turns those geometric questions into auditable row operations on the augmented matrix. Pivots expose rank and free variables; partial pivoting chooses a safer divisor and tracks row exchanges, while residual and growth checks explain why pivoting cannot repair ill-conditioning. elimination steps · pivoting and growth

Appendix.title: LU factorization and reusable solves
Appendix.Content: LU factorization and reusable solves

LU stores elimination as triangular factors. With row pivoting in this vault’s convention, ; apply the same permutation to each right-hand side, then solve one lower- and one upper-triangular system. Factorization cost is amortized across repeated solves.
Use it when: solving square general systems, especially with multiple right-hand sides.

Developed in Phase 8: The multipliers used to eliminate entries become the lower factor, while the remaining upper triangle records the reduced system; with row exchanges the convention is . Appendix.title: Symmetric positive-definite matrices and Cholesky
Appendix.Content: Symmetric positive-definite matrices and Cholesky

A real symmetric matrix is positive definite if every nonzero has positive quadratic energy . Then with nonsingular triangular . Positive semidefinite permits zero energy directions and may be singular, so Cholesky’s assumptions and failure status must be respected.
Use it when: covariance, Gram systems, energy minimization, or an SPD solve is established.

Developed in Phase 8: Positive definiteness means every nonzero direction has positive quadratic energy, which permits a Cholesky factor and stable triangular solves. The continuation derives the positive pivots, then broadens to when a symmetric matrix is indefinite and explains how a failed pivot reflects the assumptions or numerical scale. Appendix.title: QR factorization and least squares
Appendix.Content: QR factorization and least squares

QR writes with orthonormal columns in and triangular . Orthogonal coordinates preserve Euclidean lengths, so least squares reduces to a triangular solve and a perpendicular residual. Householder QR is a stable dense method; Gram–Schmidt explains the geometry but can lose orthogonality.
Use it when: fitting overdetermined data with known full column rank.

Developed in Phase 8: Orthogonal transformations change coordinates without changing Euclidean lengths. QR therefore separates the fitted component, solved through triangular , from the constant perpendicular residual; the Householder construction is the stable dense route, with Gram–Schmidt retained to make the geometry visible. Householder and Givens construction · least squares and its residual

Appendix.title: Atomic publication and durability
Appendix.Content: Atomic publication and durability
Curriculum depth: Introduced · First seen: C003 · Latest development: C003
Definition and mechanism

Publishing a prepared temporary file by replacement concerns observers of the filesystem namespace. Crash durability concerns whether contents and namespace updates survive failures; it needs a specified platform/filesystem protocol. Neither follows from building a vector of bytes. The supplied AtomicFile excerpt is an unverified repository claim, not a tested durability guarantee.
Prerequisites

ListItem.Content: • Serialization — Publication persists already-specified bytes, rather than defining their format.
• Ownership and non-owning views — A mapping or publication pipeline must keep referenced bytes valid.

Appendix.Content: Used by
Update downstream uses when later chunks build on this concept.
Recall and next depth
Name the observers and failure model for an atomic guarantee.
Pending: Platform replacement semantics, flush ordering, recovery and cross-volume limits.
Source and navigation
C003 teaching chapter · Part definitions · Dependency Map
Executed POSIX durability sequence
The durability contract now has an actual syscall-level witness in tools/labs/atomic_publication_durability_lab.cpp.

The reference creates a staging file with exclusive creation, writes the complete payload, calls fsync on the file, closes it, renames it within the same directory, opens the containing directory, and calls fsync on that directory before treating publication as complete. It then verifies the final bytes and absence of the staging name. Separate tests reject a pre-existing staging file and a traversal-style final name.

This is stronger than “write temp then rename,” because rename atomicity and durable persistence are different properties. The file sync requests persistence of file contents/metadata; the directory sync requests persistence of the directory-entry change. Successful calls on CI are evidence that the operating-system/filesystem accepted that ordering. They are not a laboratory power-cut test and cannot promise identical persistence guarantees on every filesystem, storage controller, Windows API, network filesystem or production asset pipeline.

Canonical teaching code and verified repository excerpts live here. Organize by concept or subsystem, not by incoming chunk. Update existing sections when later chunks add variants, optimizations, tests, or failure handling.
For every snippet, label it as one of:

ListItem.Content: • Canonical - minimal explanatory implementation;
• Repository-verified - copied or adapted from an inspected repository location;
• Pseudocode - intentionally non-compilable structure;
• To verify - a provisional claim that must not be presented as repository fact.

Appendix.Content: Record language/version, inputs, outputs, preconditions, ownership and lifetime where relevant, complexity, failure behavior, and verification performed. Keep long repository listings out; quote only the lines needed to prove the point and link the exact anchor in Sources and Code Anchors.md.
M001 - Width-safe fields and LSB-first bit packing
Kind: Canonical Introduced by: C001 / M001 Language: C++23
Contract

ListItem.Content: • Field width is 1-32; shift + width must fit a 32-bit carrier.
• Field insertion rejects values that do not fit instead of silently truncating them.
• Bit arrays contain only 0 or 1 and are packed LSB-first within each byte.
• Unpacking rejects a requested count larger than the source capacity.

Appendix.Content: Snippet
Cost and failure behavior

Field access over a fixed carrier is constant work. Packing and unpacking are , with packed bytes. The guards make width, value range, and source-capacity failures explicit rather than allowing invalid shifts, silent field truncation, or out-of-bounds access.
Verification

Compiled with Homebrew Clang in C++23 mode using warnings as errors. Assertions covered 0xAD, field replacement, LSB-first packing, round-trip unpacking, full-width masks, and rejected oversized unpack counts. See the current task verification record; no repository implementation was claimed by this canonical snippet.
M002 - Exhaustive 8-bit addition oracle and saturation
Kind: Canonical Introduced by: C002 / M002 Language: C++23
Contract

ListItem.Content: • Inputs model two eight-bit operands plus a carry-in of 0 or 1.
• The calculation widens before retaining the architectural low byte.
• carry and overflow report unsigned and signed representability separately.
• Saturating addition clamps after widened calculation rather than allowing byte wrap.

Appendix.Content: Snippet
Cost and failure behavior

For a fixed eight-bit architecture this is constant work. Widening preserves the ninth carry bit; the overflow expression independently compares operand and result signs. Invalid carry input fails explicitly. Saturation prevents wrap but intentionally changes algebraic behavior.
Verification

Compiled with Homebrew Clang in C++23 mode and warnings as errors. An exhaustive driver checked all 131,072 (a,b,carry_in) states against independent widened unsigned and signed-range calculations, plus saturation boundaries and invalid carry rejection.
Arithmetic reconstruction helpers

These are canonical teaching implementations. The multiplication helper widens the shifting partial product before any shift; widening only the final accumulator would lose information. Division widens the partial remainder so shifting it cannot discard the extra bit. Checked signed addition proves representability before executing the operation. Mixed-sign comparison checks the lower bound as well as the upper bound.

For subtraction, reusing add8 on the complemented operand also produces the correct binary subtraction overflow predicate. Decimal arithmetic and complete instruction timing are outside this helper’s contract. The helper tests below cover its complete arithmetic input domain.
M003 - Explicit byte codecs and checked alignment
Kind: Canonical · Language: C++23 · Source: C003 / M003.

Contract: octets are eight bits; exact uint32/uint64 types must exist. Encode an unsigned 32-bit value in declared order; decode four bytes at a checked offset without typed unaligned dereferences. The input span is borrowed for the call only. Insufficient input or invalid power-of-two alignment/page shift throws invalid_argument; numeric rounding/translation overflow throws overflow_error. These functions manipulate bytes and numeric offsets; they neither allocate aligned objects nor query real page tables. Complexity is O(4) per codec and O(1) per numeric helper.

Why no reinterpret_cast load: a span may start at any byte offset; bytewise decoding avoids assuming a live aligned uint32 object and imposes the external order explicitly. memcpy into an existing aligned object can copy representation safely for appropriate types, but does not convert host byte order. std::endian and std::byteswap are optional implementation tools, not substitutes for a format contract.
Layout probe, not a wire format

Use sizeof, alignof, and offsetof on these standard-layout types to observe your compiler. Expected 12/24/16-byte results are conditional on the stated member alignments, not portable compile-time mandates. Neither object is serialized by copying its native bytes.
M003 regression driver

Compile the canonical M001/M002/M003 snippets above together with this driver; it deliberately does not execute invalid pointer accesses. Tests cover golden bytes, both codec round trips, odd byte offset, truncation/huge-offset rejection, alignment minimality and maximum-boundary behavior, page decomposition/reconstruction, and measured ABI layout.
Limits: numeric page functions are a model, not a live MMU test. This host’s layout does not establish cross-platform ABI, SIMD performance, filesystem durability, or Kairo repository behavior.
M004 - Binary interchange inspection and strict rounding laboratory

This cumulative section extends the existing driver, not a new per-chunk source file. The raw-word classifier never evaluates signaling NaNs as floats. Finite reconstruction requires the checked binary32/binary64 host. NaN numeric reconstruction is intentionally omitted because it would not preserve payload/signaling information.

Compile all cpp fences in this file in order with Clang C++23, warnings-as-errors, sanitizers, and -ffp-model=strict. The M003 main calls run_m004_lab(), defined below. Strict floating settings and a supported runtime environment are prerequisites; this is not a fast-math demonstration. See Clang floating-point controls.

Limits: no exhaustive binary32 test, live repository calls, signaling-NaN arithmetic, performance benchmarks, FTZ/DAZ mode changes, complete FPU implementation, or cross-platform payload-preservation claim. The laboratory restores rounding direction; it deliberately exercises operations that may set floating status flags and does not promise to restore those flags.
M005 - Strict arithmetic and state-update laboratory

Reuse M004’s field inspection, validated float comparison and strict assumptions. This section adds arithmetic/order demonstrations and a simplified source-shaped weighted recurrence. It calls no Kairo or Maveb API. Compile all cpp fences in order with -ffp-model=strict -ffp-contract=off; run the shared driver, which calls this section after M004.
Representation codecs and bounded file laboratory

Contract: this is a standalone teaching implementation, not a NanoQuant patch or a promised compatible production format. It requires eight-bit octets and the binary32 host checks already used by the cumulative lab. Fixed storage is int32; binary fraction count is 0–16, with int64 intermediates proved large enough. Fixed conversion uses half-away; fixed multiply/divide use nearest-even, checked narrowing and explicit zero rejection. Quantization accepts finite samples and a positive finite scale, uses nearest-even and clips to the declared small code domain before integer conversion. NaNs canonicalize in the half/BF16 converters, while tensor serialization preserves raw uint32 words.

The source-shaped tensor image fixes 28 header bytes, little-endian fields and words, nonzero dimensions, exact file length, and at most 4096 elements. It returns raw words rather than manufacturing typed objects in mapped bytes. CRC is calculated separately over specified complete bytes; no integrity field is claimed in a source repository format. These routines are bounded examples, not a complete application library.
Compile all cpp fences in order with warnings-as-errors, strict floating semantics, implicit contraction disabled, and sanitizers. The existing main calls run_m006_lab().

Limits: tests assume the M004 host format/strict environment; non-finite summation is outside these sum contracts. The weighted example is for small safe finite fixtures, not an overflow-proof general production update. No parallel atomic test, real depth-frame corpus, mesh extraction, cross-platform bit identity, performance benchmark or live repository invocation was performed.
Received completion through Part 1100

Two new complete C++23 drivers stay inline: numerical contracts and camera contracts. Source-reported external driver results are labeled separately; their missing downloads were not treated as tested artifacts.

Appendix.Content: Game Engine — Sources and Coverage

This is the source ledger for Continuous Notes/Game Engine - From First Frame to Living Worlds. It is an audit companion, not another teaching volume. Captions, selected book passages, code snapshots, and original teaching remain different evidence types.
Coverage at 6 November 2026

The requested exhaustive video pass remains in progress. A retrieved caption file is not the same as a reviewed video. Full caption read means the cleaned caption text was read; it does not mean the on-screen code or final running project was visually inspected. Partial caption review records selected timestamp ranges and supports claims only within those ranges. Not reviewed must never be silently promoted because an episode title resembles a covered topic.

Kohi’s core playlist was enumerated at 395 positions. Travis’s channel inventory captured 573 unique metadata IDs across the inspected feeds; 426 were selected as engine candidates, including the TypeScript Engine series. Cherno’s six listed series total 234 positions; another 86 channel-video candidates expand its selected set to 320. Title-based discovery is an inclusion aid, not content analysis. Feed enumeration can omit private, removed, unlisted, or otherwise inaccessible material. These are captured scope counts, not a claim to know every unpublished source.

Kohi requests encountered HTTP 429, including after a later cooldown probe; unattempted videos remain explicitly unattempted. Some Cherno videos require sign-in/age verification and were not accessed. No authenticated-account or private Patreon content was accessed.

Appendix.Content: Executable and rendering verification

The original inline runtime_lab.cpp was compiled and run with Homebrew Clang 18.1.8 using -std=c++20 -Wall -Wextra -Wpedantic -Werror; it passed its timing-partition, interpolation, stale-handle, deferred-removal, capacity, overload, and invalid-duration assertions. The exact body also passed Apple Clang 21.0.0 with AddressSanitizer and UndefinedBehaviorSanitizer. An initial Homebrew sanitizer binary did not terminate during observation and was stopped; that run is not reported as passed.

The physics numeric witness checks the stated explicit/semi-implicit/constant-acceleration results and signed impulse/momentum example. These CPU tests are limited to the saved examples. They do not validate a windowed engine, graphics API integration, a complete collision solver, audio deadlines, network behavior, or editor interactions. Final local link, fence, Mermaid, MathJax, and code-body checks are recorded in the checkpoint reports.
Continuing this one volume

Keep future game-engine lessons in Continuous Notes/Game Engine - From First Frame to Living Worlds. Record their original source and supplied curriculum part numbers, define any prerequisite at first useful appearance, then weave the material into the relevant explanation. Retain missing/partial evidence states. The next source pass should prioritize unreviewed available captions, then retry only genuinely missing tracks when access permits. Do not redownload successful files or overwrite a final snapshot with an older module draft.
Batch 001 — capped acquisition and deeper reading

This continuation selected 50 already available caption sources for deeper review and a separate queue of at most 50 missing public captions for sequential acquisition. Eight new Kohi English captions were saved; the ninth request returned HTTP 429 and acquisition stopped immediately. The remaining 41 queue entries were not requested. Internal retries were disabled, with an eight-second gap between source requests. No authenticated or private content was accessed.

50 previously sampled sources were promoted to full-caption reads after complete cleaned-text reading. Sources not fully read retain their earlier partial status; merely putting a video into a 50-item queue does not count it as completed. The eight new captions remain not reviewed. Exact source IDs, transcript hashes, actual reading extent, acquisition logs, and before snapshots are in batches/batch-001/ under the research cache. The merged work/source-audit.json governs current counts over older channel-local snapshots.

Original pixel-layout and ray-picking numerical witnesses accompany the new teaching. The saved validation report states which final checks were executed. On-screen code, external engine builds, and native whole-book Obsidian layout remain unverified.
Batch 002 — full reading and audio transcription fallback

50 previously partial sources from the saved next50 queue received full cleaned-caption reads. 49 further YouTube caption tracks were retrieved across 49 sequential caption-source requests, with an eight-second pause and no internal retries. Including the single public-audio source request, acquisition remained capped at50 sources. See batches/batch-002/attempts.json for exact outcomes; a request cap does not imply every source succeeded.

The subtitle-free Kohi introduction dHPuU-DJoBM was processed from public audio using local OpenAI Whisper base.en (package20250625, CPU). The generated49-word VTT and raw model segments are retained separately from YouTube caption tracks. The entire generated text was read. The model misrecognized the project-name ending; that uncertainty is recorded and no technical claim is inferred from it. This is a full generated-text read, not manually verified transcription or visual inspection. Source audio/model/transcript hashes and exact generation configuration are preserved. Official Whisper reference.

Per-ID full-reading records, actual text extents, original before snapshots, generated-ASR provenance, and validation reports live in batches/batch-002/. Current counts come from merged work/source-audit.json, not older channel-local status files. The exhaustive source project remains unfinished; external engine builds, GPU/network/audio behavior, and whole-book native Obsidian layout remain untested.
Batch 003 — resumed reading, sequential acquisition, and audio ASR

50 incomplete saved-caption sources were promoted to full reads from the next50 queue, which originally contained29 sampled reviews and21 unread captions. One verified full-read record from an unfinished attempt was recovered rather than reread; its stored source text/hash and findings were retained. The remaining sources were read end-to-end in this continuation.

7 English YouTube caption tracks were saved across8 sequential caption-source requests, with an eight-second gap and internal retries disabled. Requests stop on the firstHTTP429. Public audio already cached for ImGui Events was reused for the audio fallback; no new request for that audio was made. The acquisition queue was capped at49 alongside that cached source. Exact source outcomes are in batches/batch-003/attempts.json.

Local OpenAI Whisper base.en, package20250625, CPU, generated 4286 words from the cached audio. The whole generated text was read. API names, code widths, and a repeated outro remain uncertain; the generated text is not a verbatim or manually audio-verified record. It is classified separately from YouTube captions. The reviewed text spans, audio/model/VTT hashes, contextual prompt, and ASR runtime parameters are preserved. The resulting teaching distinguishes historical narrated input plumbing from current primary guidance checked in the Dear ImGui FAQ and GLFW input guide.

All source-reading receipts, original snapshots, acquisition and transcription logs, teaching drafts, merge scripts, numeric witnesses, and actual validation reports are in batches/batch-003/. The merged work/source-audit.json governs current counts. Caption/ASR reading does not establish on-screen-code inspection, external-engine execution, or native whole-book Obsidian/PDF layout. The exhaustive project remains incomplete.
Batch 004 — render graphs, UI geometry, and renderer ownership

All 50 selected saved-caption sources were read end-to-end. The original queue contained 43 unread captions and seven sampled reviews. Ten unique full reads from the interrupted work were recovered using source hashes and normalized spoken-word counts; duplicate receipts were counted once. The final two sources were completed separately and reconciled against the exact original 50-source inventory.

Sequential acquisition saved 7 English YouTube tracks from 8 requests, eight seconds apart with internal retries disabled. Request eight returned HTTP 429 and acquisition stopped; 41 further queued caption sources were not requested. Public audio for Sparky: Ultra-Fast Batch Renderer was fetched once and reused during the continuation. Caption and audio requests together were capped at 50 sources. Exact outcomes remain in batches/batch-004/attempts.json and audio-acquisition.json.

Local OpenAI Whisper base.en, package 20250625, CPU, generated 17,680 words from that audio. The complete generated text was read. Technical names, integer-width wording and narrated performance claims remain uncertain; this is generated ASR, not a YouTube caption or manually audio-verified quotation. Audio/model/transcript hashes, model parameters, contextual hint, full reading receipt and uncertainty notes remain separate. No private or authentication-restricted source was substituted.

Teaching additions are organized around engine problems, including render-pass dependencies, resource staging, rotated UI hit tests, stencil clips, shader layouts, binary resources, audio lifecycle and indexed batches. The rendergraph ordering and UI inverse-transform examples have independent numerical witnesses. Historical implementation limits and unfinished fixes remain explicit.

Reading receipts, original snapshots, acquisition/transcription logs, synthesized additions and validation reports are retained in batches/batch-004/. The merged work/source-audit.json governs current counts. Reading captions or generated text does not establish inspection of video frames, source-code correctness, engine execution, or native whole-book Obsidian/PDF layout. The exhaustive all-video project remains unfinished.

50 of the selected 50 captions now have verified full-reading receipts. Five full reads were recovered from the interrupted attempt; new receipts are retained separately and normalized into all-completed-reviews.json. Full caption reading remains distinct from visual code inspection or engine execution. Counts above govern current coverage. The exact remaining IDs stay in BATCH_STATE.json and the next-review queue.

Two sequential acquisition probes, across the interrupted and resumed attempts, each stopped on their first HTTP 429; no successful new caption or audio acquisition is claimed. The prior ASR coverage remains unchanged.

The book pass read 81 selected PDF pages across four books, with 26 source pages visually inspected. Some initial ranges revisit earlier excerpt-based teaching; this is not a claim that all 81 are first-time pages. The additional 37-page assignment has no page overlap with the initial 44. Neither pass establishes full-book coverage. Exact hashes, PDF/printed locators, reading notes and visual boundaries are retained in pdf-reviews.json and pdf-extra-reviews.json.

ListItem.Content: • Ep. 5.5: Unions — complements ### Keep renderer contracts small while the backend grows and ### From vertices to useful render operations with a historical matrix-storage representation example. Preserve the distinction between shared storage and copied return values, and qualify the union portability caveat.

• Ep. 8: Simple Renderer — maps chiefly to ## Give the renderer a clear job, then meet the graphics API, especially ### Put a rendering boundary between games and graphics APIs, #### From vertices to useful render operations, and ### Keep submitted render resources alive until their users finish. The sample illustrates submit/flush, vertex-array/index-buffer binding, indexed drawing, and a queue-consumption bug. Preserve its per-object draw-call and per-frame matrix reconstruction limits; do not present the legacy API as current Hazel behavior.

• Ep. 14: FreeImage — complements ### Make build and source organization part of maintenance and the renderer/API discussion under ## Give the renderer a clear job, then meet the graphics API. Map the external image library and its runtime dependency to build integration; map dimensions, bits per pixel, pitch, row direction, and channel interpretation to texture-data ingestion. Keep the exploratory debugging and legacy dependency explicit.

• Visualizing Physics Colliders — maps to ### Keep the standard UI optional and stateful, but name its current limits for the settings toggle, ### Keep example behavior in the example application for editor/runtime separation, and ## Give the renderer a clear job, then meet the graphics API for overlay rendering. Preserve the concrete transform construction and the unresolved opposite-side circle visibility issue.

• Ep. 4: Vectors — maps to the volume’s math and coordinate-space material, especially ### Camera and coordinate spaces and the graphics material under ## Give the renderer a clear job, then meet the graphics API. It supplies a historical vector value-semantics example; preserve the final fixes to non-mutating operators and avoid implying this source covers later direction math.

• Ep. 24: Cleaning Up and Making a Game — maps to ### Make build and source organization part of maintenance, ### Keep example behavior in the example application, ### Keep engine lifecycle separate from game-specific frame work, and ### Packaging changes the host, not the engine’s obligations. Capture the feature freeze, extraction of game-specific tile behavior, application-loop sketch, texture batch limits, and portability intent; explicitly note that Emscripten completion is not shown.

• Ep. 17: Texture Arrays — maps to #### From vertices to useful render operations and ### Keep renderer contracts small while the backend grows. The source actually uses a list of ordinary 2D texture bindings and per-vertex sampler slots, not a GPU texture-array object. Preserve the untextured color fallback, flush-on-capacity design, legacy slot count, and untested overflow path.

• Ep. 10: Optimization and Maintenance — maps to ### Make build and source organization part of maintenance, #### API abstraction has a price, #### From vertices to useful render operations, and the existing matrix/allocator correctness material. Appendix.Content: A posteriori error bounds for contractive iteration
Curriculum depth: Developed · First seen: Phase 10 · Latest development: Phase 10
Definition and mechanism

For a fixed-point iteration , suppose is a contraction with Lipschitz constant on a region containing the iterates and its fixed point. Then the remaining error is bounded by the next step divided by : . The assumption is essential; a small step alone does not prove convergence because stagnation or a failed update can also make changes tiny. In implementation, report the contraction evidence or a suitable residual bound and keep failure distinct from success. This turns an observed update into a conditional, checkable estimate rather than a guess. If and the latest step is , this bound is , conditional on the contraction proof.

Appendix.title: Algorithmic stability
Appendix.Content: Algorithmic stability
Curriculum depth: Developed · First seen: Phase 10 · Latest development: Phase 10
Definition and mechanism

A numerical problem can be sensitive even when an algorithm handles it well. Stability describes whether the finite-precision algorithm introduces only the error expected from rounding, often by showing that its output exactly solves a nearby problem. Backward stability is one useful form; forward stability asks directly how close the computed answer is to the exact answer for the original input. The claim must name its assumptions, arithmetic model, and problem class. For example, a stable linear solver can still have a large forward error on an ill-conditioned matrix. Stability therefore belongs beside conditioning, not in its place. A dot product with a small residual can still conceal an ill-conditioned problem, so report which notion of stability is actually supported.
Prerequisites

ListItem.Content: • Forward and backward error
• Conditioning and singularity

Appendix.title: Numerical error budgets
Appendix.Content: Numerical error budgets
Curriculum depth: Developed · First seen: Phase 10 · Latest development: Phase 10
Definition and mechanism

A computed result can differ from a target because of model assumptions, discretization, solver termination, arithmetic, sampling, or uncertain reference data. These contributions may interact, so an additive budget is a diagnostic model rather than a universal identity. First identify which errors are deterministic bounds, which are observed estimates, and which are stochastic uncertainty. For example, a ray-traced pixel can combine approximation of geometry, finite sample variance, floating-point accumulation, and an imperfect reference image. Allocate effort where the dominant contribution lies: extra precision cannot fix model bias, and more samples cannot repair an incorrect PDF. Report units and assumptions with every tolerance.

Definition and mechanism
Under nearest binary rounding the conventional relative bound for normal-range results is u=2^-p, half upward epsilon. For binary32 this is 2^-24. The bound has range/rounding assumptions.
Repeated-rounding bounds use when , under the stated rounding and range assumptions. Summation error also depends on operand magnitudes; this is not a universal relative-error guarantee.

Appendix.title: Accumulated rounding error

Curriculum depth: Introduced · First seen: C005 · Latest development: Phase 10
Definition and mechanism

Appendix.title: Finite differences and step-size balance
Appendix.Content: Finite differences and step-size balance
Curriculum depth: Developed · First seen: Phase 9 · Latest development: Phase 9
Definition and mechanism

Finite differences estimate derivatives from sampled function values. Forward and backward differences use one-sided samples and have first-order truncation error; central differences use samples on both sides and usually have second-order truncation error for smooth functions. Making the step arbitrarily small is not always better: subtractive cancellation and evaluation noise grow as the step shrinks, while truncation error grows when it is too large. The useful step balances these effects and depends on scale, precision, and function noise. Finite differences are valuable for black-box sensitivities and gradient checks, but they are not automatic differentiation and can fail near discontinuities or branch changes. A numerical gradient check should compare directional derivatives, use scale-aware steps, and avoid interpreting one tolerance pass as proof that every derivative path is correct.
Prerequisites

ListItem.Content: • Derivative as a local linear map
• Absolute and relative error

Appendix.title: Numerical quadrature and error
Appendix.Content: Numerical quadrature and error
Curriculum depth: Developed · First seen: Phase 9 · Latest development: Phase 9
Definition and mechanism

Quadrature approximates a definite integral from finitely many function evaluations. Left, right, and midpoint rectangle rules use constant local models; the trapezoid rule uses linear interpolation; Simpson’s rule integrates a local quadratic fit over paired intervals. Their errors depend on smoothness, interval size, and rule-specific derivative bounds. Refining the mesh usually improves accuracy for smooth functions, but increases computation and may expose floating-point accumulation error. Adaptive quadrature places more samples where the integrand changes rapidly, provided its error estimator is trustworthy. Quadrature differs from Monte Carlo: deterministic rules have dimension-dependent behavior, while random sampling is attractive in high dimensions but has statistical uncertainty. Report the interval, nodes, weights, stopping tolerance, and error-control method so numerical results can be reproduced.
Prerequisites

Appendix.title: Bracketed and open root solvers
Appendix.Content: Bracketed and open root solvers
Curriculum depth: Developed · First seen: Phase 10 · Latest development: Phase 10
Definition and mechanism

A root solver seeks . A bracketed method maintains an interval whose endpoints have opposite signs; continuity then guarantees at least one root remains inside, and bisection provides a predictable shrinking error bound. Open methods such as secant and Newton can converge faster near a well-behaved simple root, but they may diverge, encounter a zero derivative, or leave the relevant domain. A safeguarded hybrid uses a bracket for global protection and accepts fast proposals only when they preserve progress. Residual size alone does not certify root accuracy when the root is poorly conditioned, and discontinuous functions do not satisfy the sign-change guarantee.

• Conditioning and singularity

Appendix.title: Stable quadratic root evaluation
Appendix.Content: Stable quadratic root evaluation
Curriculum depth: Developed · First seen: Phase 10 · Latest development: Phase 10
Definition and mechanism

The direct quadratic formula can lose nearly all significant digits in one root when it subtracts nearly equal values. For real coefficients with nonzero leading coefficient and a valid nonnegative discriminant, compute a signed large-magnitude numerator first: , then obtain roots as and . The second root follows from the product relation . This avoids cancellation in the small root, but it does not prevent overflow in the discriminant or cover degenerate coefficients, nonfinite inputs, or ; a robust solver also scales inputs and handles those cases explicitly. For example, the small root of is near , exactly the root most endangered by direct subtraction.

Appendix.title: Definite integrals and the fundamental theorem
Appendix.source: Concepts/Definite integrals and the fundamental theorem.md
Appendix.Content: Definite integrals and the fundamental theorem
Curriculum depth: Developed · First seen: Phase 9 · Latest development: Phase 9
Definition and mechanism

A definite integral accumulates a quantity over an interval, with sign and units determined by the integrand and integration variable. Riemann sums approximate this accumulation by weighted samples; under suitable regularity conditions their limit defines the integral. The fundamental theorem connects accumulation and differentiation: an antiderivative evaluates the net integral, and the derivative of an accumulated integral recovers its integrand when continuity conditions hold. This link explains why integrating velocity gives displacement and why a variable upper-limit integral solves a simple differential equation. Definite integral, indefinite antiderivative, and geometric area are related but not interchangeable ideas. The integration variable is a dummy variable, so name it distinctly from the endpoint. Integrals also form the target of Monte Carlo estimators, where measure and sampling density must match.
Prerequisites

Appendix.title: Stateful pseudorandom generators and stream state
Appendix.source: Concepts/Stateful pseudorandom generators and stream state.md
Appendix.Content: Stateful pseudorandom generators and stream state
Curriculum depth: Developed · First seen: Phase 10 · Latest development: Phase 10
Definition and mechanism

A pseudorandom-number generator is a deterministic state transition plus an output rule. With a fixed engine, seed, and call order, its integer sequence is reproducible; it is not a source of mathematical independence by itself. Linear congruential generators are compact but have lattice and low-bit structure that can make multidimensional samples poor. Larger-state engines trade memory for period and other statistical properties. Parallel programs need an explicit stream strategy: shared state couples samples to thread scheduling, while copied seeds can duplicate streams. Reproducibility requires recording algorithm version, state, seed derivation, distribution mapping, and sampling order. Standard-library distributions may not yield identical transformed sequences across implementations. Simulation generators are not cryptographically secure unless specifically designed for that purpose.
Prerequisites

ListItem.Content: • Common probability distributions and their assumptions

Algebraic equivalence is not numerical equivalence

Two formulas can be identical over real arithmetic and behave very differently in finite precision. Stable reformulation changes the computational path while preserving the intended mathematical quantity.
For the quadratic equation, the textbook root expression can subtract nearly equal numbers and lose most significant digits. Computing one root with a sign-aware expression such as
and obtaining the other as avoids that cancellation in many cases.

The same idea appears in log-sum-exp, hypot-style norms, rationalizing expressions, compensated sums, and solving least squares with QR rather than normal equations. A reformulation is not automatically stable: its overflow/underflow regions and exceptional inputs still need analysis.

Tests should compare against a higher-precision reference across adversarial inputs, not only ordinary random values. The goal is to show that the reformulated algorithm reduces forward/backward error where the naive expression is fragile.

Appendix.title: Taylor models and approximation error
Appendix.Content: Taylor models and approximation error
Curriculum depth: Developed · First seen: Phase 9 · Latest development: Phase 9
Definition and mechanism

A Taylor model approximates a smooth function near a reference point using its value, derivatives, and higher-order terms. The first-order model is the derivative’s linear map; the second-order model adds curvature through the Hessian. A remainder term describes what the finite truncation omits, so local accuracy depends on step size and higher derivatives over the region. Big-O notation gives an asymptotic scale, while a concrete error bound needs assumptions such as bounded derivatives. Taylor models power local optimization, camera Jacobian updates, uncertainty propagation, and numerical error analysis. They are not reliable far from the expansion point merely because the polynomial is easy to evaluate. When the input distribution is broad or crosses a singularity, first-order covariance propagation can miss bias and tail behavior; validate or replace the local model.
Prerequisites

• Hessians and local curvature

Appendix.title: Hessians and local curvature
Appendix.Content: Hessians and local curvature
Curriculum depth: Developed · First seen: Phase 9 · Latest development: Phase 9
Definition and mechanism

The Hessian collects second partial derivatives of a scalar objective. It describes how the gradient changes and supplies the quadratic term in a local Taylor model. For a smooth scalar field, the Hessian is symmetric under the usual equality-of-mixed-partials assumptions. Its eigenvectors indicate local curvature directions: positive eigenvalues give upward curvature, negative values downward curvature, and near-zero values weakly constrained directions. A positive-definite Hessian supports a strict local minimum in the unconstrained setting, while an indefinite Hessian signals a saddle-like local model. The Hessian is not the same as the curvature of an embedded geometric surface, though both involve second-order change. In optimization, exact Newton steps solve with the Hessian; practical methods may regularize or approximate it because conditioning, cost, or indefiniteness can make direct steps unreliable.

Appendix.title: Conditional Gaussians and Schur complements
Appendix.Content: Conditional Gaussians and Schur complements
Curriculum depth: Developed · First seen: Phase 10 · Latest development: Phase 10
Definition and mechanism

Conditioning one block of a jointly Gaussian vector on another produces a Gaussian conditional law under the usual nonsingular assumptions. Its mean shifts by the cross-covariance times the inverse observed-block covariance, while its covariance is the Schur complement Σbb−ΣbaΣaa⁻¹Σab. That conditional covariance is positive semidefinite: insert the vector (−Σaa⁻¹Σabv,v) into the joint covariance quadratic form. If the joint covariance is positive definite, the Schur complement is positive definite. The conditional covariance does not depend on the observed value, although the conditional mean does. This formula links Bayesian updating, Gaussian elimination, and block linear systems. Singular observed blocks require a compatible degenerate-Gaussian treatment or a rank-revealing method; blindly applying an inverse is invalid.
Prerequisites

ListItem.Content: • Multivariate Gaussian distributions and whitening
• Gaussian elimination and pivoting

Appendix.title: Uniform shuffling without replacement
Appendix.Content: Uniform shuffling without replacement
Curriculum depth: Developed · First seen: Phase 10 · Latest development: Phase 10
Definition and mechanism

Fisher–Yates generates a uniform permutation by walking from the last array element downward and choosing an index uniformly from the unshuffled prefix. Each permutation has probability if every bounded integer choice is unbiased and the random source meets its assumptions. A common error is to use a random integer routine with modulo bias; another is to draw from the wrong interval and omit permutations. For a fixed input array, test that the output contains every original element once; statistical tests can supplement, but not replace, deterministic checks of bounds and uniqueness. The same primitive supports uniform sample subsets and randomized stratification.

Appendix.title: Stateless keyed sampling and reproducibility
Appendix.Content: Stateless keyed sampling and reproducibility
Curriculum depth: Developed · First seen: Phase 10 · Latest development: Phase 10
Definition and mechanism

Stateless sampling derives an output from explicit coordinates such as a master seed, pixel, sample index, and dimension. The same key can be recomputed without replaying prior generator calls, which makes debugging and parallel scheduling easier. A hash mixer can provide deterministic, well-dispersed values, but reproducibility does not prove IID behavior or statistical quality. Counter-based generators use designed mixing rounds and can provide stronger parallel-stream properties under their analyzed models. Distinct sampling dimensions reduce accidental reuse, yet a dimension map must remain stable when code changes. Record the key layout, algorithm, version, and conversion to floating point. Test multidimensional patterns and estimator convergence; a good one-dimensional histogram does not establish good joint behavior.

Definition and mechanism

SIMD applies an operation across multiple data lanes; GPU buffers and formats specify how values are arranged for parallel access. Packing can reduce traffic but adds decoding and alignment constraints. Lane layout, alignment, and access grouping require later treatment.
Prerequisites

ListItem.Content: • Machine word — A processor’s natural integer processing width is often called its word width, but the term is architecture dependent.
• Alignment and padding — Alignment is a required address multiple for an object.

Packed structures and misaligned access may save space but introduce boundary crossings; Field reordering and AoS versus SoA can improve fieldwise access. CPU ABI layout is not automatically a GPU buffer schema.

Appendix.title: Directional and total derivatives
Appendix.Content: Directional and total derivatives
Curriculum depth: Developed · First seen: Phase 9 · Latest development: Phase 9
Definition and mechanism

A directional derivative measures first-order change along a chosen direction. For a differentiable scalar field, it is the gradient paired with that direction; for a vector map, the Jacobian acts on the direction. The total derivative accounts for every input coordinate changing according to a path, combining partial derivatives with the rates of the coordinates themselves. A direction need not be normalized: normalization changes whether the derivative is per unit distance or per unit parameter. This distinction matters in signed-distance queries, motion paths, and parameterized camera projections. The total derivative clarifies the chain rule: if a state depends on time and an output depends on that state, the time rate is the local derivative composed with the state velocity. These are local statements, not global linearity claims.
Prerequisites

ListItem.Content: • Partial derivatives and gradients
• Derivative as a local linear map

Appendix.title: Partial derivatives and gradients
Appendix.Content: Partial derivatives and gradients
Curriculum depth: Developed · First seen: Phase 9 · Latest development: Phase 9
Definition and mechanism

For a function of several inputs, a partial derivative varies one coordinate while holding the others fixed. Collecting these derivatives gives the gradient for a scalar-valued function. The gradient is a covector of first-order sensitivities: its pairing with a small displacement predicts the scalar change. Under the Euclidean inner product, the gradient vector points in the direction of steepest ascent, and its negative gives steepest local descent. Coordinate scaling changes derivative magnitudes and can therefore change optimization behavior. A partial derivative is not generally the full effect when inputs move together; that requires the total derivative or directional derivative. In graphics, gradients describe image sensitivity to geometry or material parameters, while their coordinates must be interpreted with the parameter units and basis used by the model.
Prerequisites

• Derivative as a local linear map

Appendix.title: Vault Repair and Source Retention - 2026-11-14
Appendix.Content: Vault repair and source retention — 14 November 2026

This is the supervised local repair of the active iCloud/Obsidian Master vault, beginning at commit c142869a391c32d55068ddfbf4d4ac11ce52762c. The vault’s existing hidden .obsidian configuration and unrelated Finder/workspace edits are left in place. The three continuous books remain the teaching surface; this record tracks changes and evidence, not a fourth lesson book.
Integrated teaching and code comments

Computing Foundations now embeds its temporary-lifetime, SE(3) exp/log and paired-inference witnesses at their teaching seams. The misplaced closing fence after the reverse-mode Tape includes is removed, keeping the class inside its C++ block. The statistical witness validates finite inputs, normalizes its sign-flip comparison and checks measurement-unit rescaling; the pose witness exercises its documented near-pi rejection.

Graphics now embeds the planar eight-state EKF, 3-D zero-order-hold IMU preintegration and discrete NeRF volume-rendering witnesses. The planar camera is explicitly co-located and aligned with the body. The original 1,842-line perceptual/XR packet is relocated intact after rendering so the mathematical prerequisites precede it. The relocation itself preserves 240,779 characters exactly; earlier wiki-route corrections are recorded separately.

Game Engine now embeds the block contact, symbolic subresource-state, rollback, audio and AI witnesses. The new bounded scene-persistence example teaches explicit versioned fields, strict decimal input, stable IDs, forward references, iterative cycle rejection, migration and candidate-then-swap publication. Negative fixtures prove failed loads keep the live scene unchanged. This is an in-memory schema/transaction witness, not filesystem durability or a production scene format.

For these added and revised programs, implementation reasoning, state meanings, units, branch choices and limits are explained in comments beside the relevant operations. Conceptual prerequisites remain before code. Existing teaching elsewhere was preserved; this pass does not claim to have re-commented every historical snippet.
Navigation, formatting and supervision

Retired Mathematics, XR and Systems wiki targets now lead to the actual canonical books, retaining labels and anchors. Four dangling concept links point to existing developed explanations rather than new glossary stubs. The retired rigid-body route resolves to the preserved Foundations section.

Independent small-agent reviews exposed the missing camera/body extrinsic assumption, scale-dependent statistical tie tolerance, nonfinite-data handling and an untested near-pi branch; those findings were repaired before final verification. Five existing concept cards also had control-byte/missing-command corruption in TeX. Their GGX/Fresnel, homology, spherical harmonics, impulse/friction and Beer–Lambert formulas were repaired with units and domain assumptions.

The source guard compares complete parsed code blocks, including comments, instead of relying on a common first include line or counting only one fence style. The preservation guard pins the actual pre-repair books and permits only the documented route, Tape-fence, closure-statement and intact-XR-relocation changes. It still rejects removal or reordering of other prior teaching.

The final-pass workflows now have read-only repository permissions and verify the checked-in books. They no longer apply or push repairs. Appendix.title: Multiple importance sampling
Appendix.Content: Multiple importance sampling
Multiple importance sampling combines estimators from several sampling techniques without pretending that one proposal distribution is good everywhere.

Suppose two techniques generate the same contribution using PDFs and . With one sample from each technique, an MIS estimator can use weights and satisfying appropriate partition and support conditions. The balance heuristic uses
with the symmetric definition for . For one sample from each, .

The key idea is not “average two answers.” The estimator must evaluate the PDFs in the same measure for the same sampled event. Mixing a solid-angle PDF with an area PDF without the Jacobian conversion makes the weights meaningless.
Support matters

If technique A can sample a contribution that B cannot, then at that event and A should receive full weight. But if the implementation accidentally reports zero because it evaluated the wrong lobe, wrong hemisphere, or wrong light-selection probability, MIS can hide a bug behind a numerically finite result.
For direct lighting, the full light-sampling PDF may include both discrete light selection and continuous point/direction sampling:
The BSDF PDF must be converted to the same directional measure before comparison.
Power heuristic
A common alternative is
often with . This suppresses a technique more aggressively when its PDF is much smaller than the competing proposal.
The heuristic changes variance, not the target integral, when the estimator is constructed correctly.
Executable reference

tools/labs/monte_carlo_transport_lab.cpp checks the simple balance-weight partition property and separately verifies cosine-hemisphere transport and Russian-roulette expectation compensation. It is a mathematical estimator witness, not yet a complete path tracer with next-event estimation and scene lights.
Read the connected derivation at Continuous Notes/University - Worlds, Images and Inference - Graphics, Vision and Photography#Follow one path without losing its probability.
Related: Russian roulette path termination, Inverse, rejection, and importance sampling, Sampling support and missing strata.
Scene-level MIS witness

tools/labs/path_transport_scene_lab.cpp lifts the estimator checks into an actual camera/geometry/shading path. A camera ray intersects a sphere, establishes the shading normal, and evaluates Lambertian outgoing radiance under a constant environment using two proposals for the same hemisphere integral: uniform-hemisphere light sampling and cosine-weighted BSDF sampling. Each sample evaluates both PDFs in the same solid-angle measure and uses the balance heuristic.
Because constant environment radiance over a Lambertian surface has the analytic solution

the pixel estimate has an independent target rather than merely comparing two noisy implementations. The witness therefore checks geometry, throughput, proposal PDFs, MIS weighting and convergence together. Emissive-geometry NEE, multiple bounces, media and full rendered-image parity remain later evidence layers.

Appendix.title: Shader buffer ABI
Appendix.Content: Shader buffer ABI

A shader buffer is a binary interface between independently compiled code. CPU and shader code must agree on member offsets, element widths, alignment, array stride, matrix layout, and total record stride. “These structs have the same fields” is not enough.

Suppose a record logically contains a 3-vector followed by a scalar. The mathematical payload is four floats, but the ABI may impose an alignment boundary for the vector or the containing record. The only safe statement is the one established by the layout rules and, ideally, reflection/compiled shader metadata.
Layout is a function of context

Different interfaces can have different rules: vertex attributes, constant/uniform buffers, storage buffers, argument buffers and push/root constants are not interchangeable contracts. Matrix row/column-major convention is another independent dimension.

On the CPU side, standard C++ object layout also has rules about padding and alignment. Copying bytes from a native struct into a shader buffer is valid only when the native representation is deliberately made compatible or explicit serialization writes the expected offsets.
Verify rather than guess
A robust pipeline should generate or reflect a machine-readable layout description and compare it with CPU declarations:

ListItem.Content: • expected offset for every member;
• expected array stride;
• matrix stride and orientation;
• record size/alignment;
• scalar widths and signedness.

Appendix.Content: Static assertions can catch CPU layout changes. Shader reflection or compiler metadata catches shader-side changes. A golden byte dump can test the complete bridge.
Failure modes

Common failures include using a 12-byte mental model for a vector type whose ABI slot is 16 bytes, mixing bool widths, assuming packed enums, copying pointer-containing structs, row/column-major disagreement, and updating one side of the interface without rebuilding the other.
Teach and reconstruct: Continuous Notes/Computing Foundations - From Bits to C++ and Systems APIs#Make a shader record an explicit binary contract.
Related: Alignment and padding, GPU vertex specification, Tensor runtime layout and views.

Appendix.title: HMAC and HKDF
Appendix.Content: HMAC and HKDF
HMAC authenticates a message under a shared secret key. HKDF uses HMAC to turn input keying material into one or more pseudorandom-looking keys with explicit context separation.
Extract then expand
HKDF has two conceptual stages.
Extract computes a pseudorandom key:
Expand derives output keying material in blocks:
Concatenate blocks until the requested output length is reached.

The info field is not decoration. It lets the same root keying material derive separate keys for different purposes, versions, peers or directions. Domain separation reduces accidental cross-protocol key reuse.
A salt can improve extraction and should follow the protocol design. HKDF does not create entropy that is absent from the input keying material.
Evidence
tools/labs/crypto_primitives_lab.cpp validates HMAC-SHA256 against RFC 4231 and HKDF-SHA256 extract/expand against RFC 5869 test vectors.
That proves the bit-level reference on those vectors. It does not establish side-channel resistance, secret erasure, key storage, protocol context selection or application security.
Primary standards: RFC 2104 / RFC 4231 for HMAC testing and RFC 5869 for HKDF.
Related: Integrity and authenticity, Checksums CRCs and hashes.

Appendix.title: Merkle trees and authenticated structure
Appendix.Content: Merkle trees and authenticated structure

A Merkle tree hashes data into leaves and repeatedly hashes child digests into parent digests until one root remains. The root commits to the entire ordered leaf set under the collision-resistance assumptions of the hash and the tree encoding.
A safe design domain-separates leaves from internal nodes, for example:
Without an unambiguous encoding, different logical tree structures can accidentally serialize to the same byte concatenation before hashing.
Inclusion proof

To prove that one leaf belongs to a tree, provide the sibling hash at each level and the left/right ordering bits. The verifier starts from the leaf hash and reconstructs the root. Proof size is for a balanced binary tree.
The trusted root must come from a trusted channel or authenticated record. A Merkle proof checked against an attacker-provided root proves nothing about authenticity.
Odd leaf policy
When a level has an odd number of nodes, the format must specify what happens: duplicate the last node, promote it, or use another encoding. Different policies create different roots.

tools/labs/crypto_primitives_lab.cpp uses an explicit domain-separated construction and duplicates the last digest on odd levels. The test proves determinism and that changing one sample leaf changes the root in the exercised case.
Related: Checksums CRCs and hashes, Integrity and authenticity.

Appendix.title: Shamir secret sharing
Appendix.Content: Shamir secret sharing

Shamir secret sharing splits a secret into shares so that any threshold number can reconstruct it while fewer shares reveal no information in the ideal finite-field construction when coefficients are chosen uniformly at random.
Choose a prime field containing the secret value and a threshold . Construct a random polynomial
with secret . Give participant the share for distinct nonzero .
Any shares recover through Lagrange interpolation:
Every division is multiplication by a finite-field inverse. Ordinary integer division is wrong.
Security condition

The coefficients must be generated with a cryptographically secure random generator. Deterministic or predictable coefficients destroy the information-theoretic secrecy claim even though interpolation still reconstructs correctly.
Share identifiers also matter: using duplicate x coordinates makes interpolation invalid.
Evidence boundary
tools/labs/crypto_primitives_lab.cpp demonstrates a three-share reconstruction over prime field 257 and reconstructs the same secret from two different three-share subsets.
Its polynomial coefficients are deliberately deterministic so the test is reproducible. Therefore the laboratory proves interpolation arithmetic, not production secrecy.
A production system additionally needs CSPRNG coefficients, authenticated share transport/storage, versioning, participant identity, compromise/recovery policy and secure erasure.
Related: Integrity and authenticity, HMAC and HKDF.

Appendix.title: Floating-point canonicalization
Appendix.Content: Floating-point canonicalization
Curriculum depth: Developed · First seen: C004 · Latest development: C006
Definition and mechanism

Canonicalization deliberately merges encodings: both zeros to positive zero, all NaNs to one quiet pattern. Raw preservation instead keeps sign/payload distinctions. Neither is universally correct; this is a file/hash contract choice.

M006’s BF16 converter explicitly canonicalizes NaNs while its raw tensor codec preserves uint32 payload words. These are distinct contracts: numerical closeness, canonical identity and raw byte identity must not be conflated.
Prerequisites

ListItem.Content: • Signed zero — Numerical equality merges two encodings and must be reflected in the chosen ordering or byte policy.
• NaNs and payloads — Unordered comparisons and payload distinctions require explicit metric, comparison and serialization policy.
• Serialization — Changing canonical representation changes the external byte contract.
• Bit casting and representation — A representation word must be distinguished from a numeric conversion before canonicalization.

Appendix.Content: Groupwise quantization and metadata
Curriculum depth: Developed · First seen: C006 · Latest development: C006
Definition and mechanism

Reconstruction depth

Groupwise quantization divides a tensor into blocks and assigns quantization parameters per block rather than per entire tensor. For affine quantization, a group may store scale and zero point so that .

The group size controls a three-way trade: smaller groups follow local distributions more accurately but increase metadata bandwidth and reduce the work sharing one scale; larger groups amortize metadata and simplify vector kernels but increase approximation error when values have heterogeneous ranges.

Metadata is part of the runtime format. A decoder needs the exact grouping axis and order, group length, code width, scale type, zero-point type, tail policy, alignment and byte order. A mismatch can produce plausible but entirely wrong model outputs.

Benchmarking should report payload plus metadata bytes and measure the real dequantized dot-product kernel rather than only offline reconstruction error. The best group size depends on cache behavior, SIMD width, memory bandwidth and model sensitivity.

Appendix.title: Atomic operations and write contention
Appendix.Content: Atomic operations and write contention
Curriculum depth: Developed · First seen: C001 · Latest development: C005
Definition and mechanism
Independently meaningful fields sharing a word can require coordinated read-modify-write and can cause unrelated writers to contend.

An atomic update is indivisible to other participating accesses under its specified memory ordering. Packed independent flags may share one read-modify-write location: writers can overwrite each other without coordination. Contention means accesses compete for ownership or serialization.

Atomic additions can prevent lost writes without fixing addition order. Different valid schedules can produce different rounded sums; deterministic reduction requires a defined tree as well as safe synchronization.
Prerequisites

ListItem.Content: • Bit packing — Packing places several constrained values into a carrier.
• Machine word — A processor’s natural integer processing width is often called its word width, but the term is architecture dependent.

Appendix.Content: Used by

ListItem.Content: • Numerical reproducibility — Indivisible updates do not impose a unique schedule-independent ordering.

Why clipping a contribution changes the estimator
A capped weighted update replaces an unbounded contribution with something like

The cap protects an online system from one extreme weight dominating state, overflowing finite precision, or creating intolerable variance. But unless the cap is part of the intended mathematical model, it introduces bias: contributions above the threshold are deliberately underrepresented.

This trade appears in importance weighting, robust online statistics, adaptive reconstruction and control. The correct question is not “does clipping stabilize it?” but how bias changes as the cap moves and whether the uncapped tail is real signal, model mismatch, or corrupted data.

A useful experiment sweeps , records variance, bias against an uncapped/high-precision reference, effective sample size and downstream failure rate. Tests should include weights exactly at the cap, negative/invalid weights when the domain forbids them, and extreme values that would overflow the uncapped path.

Appendix.title: Convergence order and Richardson extrapolation
Appendix.Content: Convergence order and Richardson extrapolation
Curriculum depth: Developed · First seen: Phase 10 · Latest development: Phase 10
Definition and mechanism

If an approximation has leading error , halving the step reduces that term by about . Comparing results at , , and estimates the observed order; Richardson extrapolation combines two resolutions to cancel the leading term when the assumed order is valid. The method is diagnostic, not magic: measurements must be in the asymptotic regime, the same mathematical quantity must be computed at each resolution, and roundoff or stochastic noise must not dominate. For Euler integration, first-order refinement predicts the leading error to halve. Record the sequence and residuals rather than reporting an order from one pair alone. Ratios near an expected power provide evidence, but one noisy ratio is not a convergence study.
Prerequisites

ListItem.Content: • Discretization, truncation, and roundoff
• Finite differences and step-size balance
• Numerical quadrature and error

Appendix.title: Argument-dependent lookup
Appendix.Content: Argument-dependent lookup
Curriculum depth: Introduced · First seen: C007 · Latest development: C007
Definition and mechanism

For a suitable unqualified function call, argument types contribute associated namespaces/classes to candidate lookup. dot(a,b) can find geometry::dot for geometry::Pair arguments. using std::swap; swap(a,b) combines a fallback with custom ADL candidates. Some ordinary lookup results suppress ADL.

Appendix.title: Guest and host integer domains
Appendix.Content: Guest and host integer domains
Curriculum depth: Forward · First seen: C002 · Latest development: C002
Definition and mechanism
An emulator may compute an -bit guest operation in a wider host type so carry and other discarded architectural information remain observable.

Guest means the machine being emulated; host means the implementation platform. An eight-bit guest addition can use a host temporary holding 0–511, extract carry, then narrow to 0–255. Host signed overflow must never be used to imitate guest wrap.
Prerequisites

ListItem.Content: • Fixed-width integer types — When supplied, std::uint32_t has exactly 32 bits; uint_least32_t has at least 32; uint_fast32_t is chosen for speed with at least 32.
• Carry, overflow, negative, and zero flags — For eight-bit addition, C tests exact sum>255; V tests signed sum outside [−128,127]; N is result bit 7; Z tests low result==0.

Appendix.Content: Borrow contracts and pool epochs
Curriculum depth: Introduced · First seen: C008 · Latest development: C008
Definition and mechanism

An epoch versions a borrow-validity interval. A checked borrow compares its saved epoch to the live pool counter before using the cached element. The pool counter must outlive the borrow; counters alone do not supply ownership, synchronization, race freedom or wrap immunity.

Appendix.Content: Memory-mapped files
Curriculum depth: Introduced · First seen: C003 · Latest development: C003
Definition and mechanism

A file mapping makes file-backed bytes accessible through a virtual region. Fault handling can supply pages lazily; ownership, access flags, mapping length, and synchronization still matter. A mapped byte buffer is not automatically a set of live aligned C++ objects. File persistence and virtual access are separate mechanisms.
